subject: Hosted usage increase & term alignment discussion
messages:
From: Lucy Harper <lucy@greenline-retail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Grant Miller <grant@greenline-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted usage increase — possible term/price alignment?

Hi Aditya,

Hope you're well. Quick note from our engineering and ops teams — since launching the new recommendations pipeline two months ago our monthly token consumption has spiked well beyond projections. We're attaching a brief usage extract for July.

Current situation:
- Baseline commit: 500M tokens/month (hosted)
- July observed: ~1.35B tokens (bursty traffic around promotions)
- We expect higher sustained usage through Q4 (seasonal + new features)

We want to discuss options to avoid throttling and to secure predictable pricing for the next 12 months. Specifically:
1) A raised monthly commit (suggested 1.5B) with corresponding unit price
2) Any soft-throttle/overage protection we can get while we finalize forecasts
3) Term length vs. discount trade-offs (12 vs 24 months)

Can you share possible pathways and ops requirements? Grant and I are available next week for a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Lucy
Director of Engineering
Greenline Retail

Attachment: Greenline_Usage_Report_July2025.csv (csv, 68KB)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Harper <lucy@greenline-retail.com>
Cc: Grant Miller <grant@greenline-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted usage increase — possible term/price alignment?

Hi Lucy — thanks for the note and the report. Appreciate the context and the heads-up on Q4.

High-level thoughts before a call:
- We can support a raised hosted commit to 1.5B tokens/month under our Hosted plan. Two levers we commonly use: a) step-up commit (12 month with scheduled increases) or b) a flat higher commit with a modest volume discount.
- Soft-throttle options: we can configure a grace overage band (up to +15% tokens) with dynamic soft-throttling signals rather than hard rate limits — useful for promotion spikes.
- Term/discount trade-offs: 12-months standard vs 24-months for an additional 6–10% effective discount depending on commit size.

I'll loop in Marissa on pricing and Karthik on ops/throughput to ensure we capture any constraints (latency SLOs, prefix caching, burst capacity). Can you confirm whether Greenline wants predictable monthly billing (committed spend) or prefers commit + overage billing?

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick technical sync (15–30m) with your SREs to review traffic profile and acceptable throttling behavior
2) Pricing options doc with 2–3 tiers we can sign to move forward
3) Ops checklist for onboarding raised commit into production (KV cache tuning, burst pool sizing)

Available times Tue/Wed 9–11am PT — let me know what works.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Harper <lucy@greenline-retail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Aug 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted usage increase — possible term/price alignment?

Lucy / team — following up from Aditya's note and the quick call yesterday. We put together a concise proposal attached (RI_Upsell_Proposal_4.pdf). Highlights below: 

Proposal summary (three options):
A) Conservative step-up (12 mo): 750M -> 1.0B -> 1.5B monthly commits across quarter milestones; incremental unit price reduction of 3% at each step; no prepaid requirement.
B) Flat uplift (12 mo): single committed tier at 1.5B tokens/month; 8% volume discount vs current list; 30-day soft overage band (+15%) with soft-throttle signaling.
C) Committed + term (24 mo): commit 1.5B tokens/month for 24 months; 14% effective discount and priority burst pool allocation during promotions.

Operational notes (Karthik / Priyom):
- Burst capacity: to support promotional peaks we recommend enabling the burst pool with a 20% buffer for first 60 days while we observe traffic patterns.
- Latency SLOs: current benchmarks meet your 95th percentile targets; if you increase prompt lengths or concurrent sessions we may need a tuning window.
- Onboarding tasks: update billing PO, sign amendment, schedule a handoff call with our Ops team (1–2 hours), and apply routing policy for primary/backup region.

Next steps we need from Greenline:
1) Preferred option (A/B/C) and target go-live month
2) PO or procurement contact for billing
3) Access to an SRE contact for the ops handoff call

Attachment: RI_Upsell_Proposal_4.pdf (pdf, 115KB)

Thanks — happy to tighten any numbers once you indicate the option you prefer.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Grant Miller <grant@greenline-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucy Harper <lucy@greenline-retail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted usage increase — possible term/price alignment?

Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the clear options and the proposal. We reviewed internally and want to proceed with Option C (24-month commit at 1.5B/month) pending final pricing table and a brief legal redline. A few quick asks so we can get procurement moving: 

1) Can you produce a one-page pricing table that explicitly shows monthly committed spend, unit price, and the expected monthly invoice amount?
2) We need DocuSign-ready amendment and target effective date of 2025-10-01.
3) For the burst pool allocation, can you confirm the priority level (we need a written SLA note confirming priority over non-committed burst traffic during promotion windows)?

We'll share procurement contact (procurement@greenline-retail.com) and loop them into DocuSign once we have the final numbers. Please send the pricing table and amendment this week.

Thanks,
Grant
VP, Platform Engineering
Greenline Retail
